Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up

  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element

  tab-list                    list all tabs

  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs

  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.

Inspected the three files; no edits made.

### Architecture and current mechanics
- **`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`** is a single IIFE. Its central persisted object is `state`, initialized by `defaultState()` and restored by `loadState()` using `SAVE_KEY = 'stillwater-cultivator-v1'` (lines 2, 23–35). `render()` updates the cultivation dashboard and calls `renderSubView()`; `tick()` advances the game once per second (lines 71–111, 252–270).
- Cultivation is currently **one linear path**: `state.stage`, `realmBands`, `requirement()`, `realmTitle()`, `breakChance()`, and `attemptBreak()` govern progression (lines 3–10, 57–65, 117, 163–190). The dashboard’s control/spirit/body stats are derived values in `render()` (lines 87–92), not independently advancing paths.
- The five existing views are Cultivate, Techniques, Expeditions, Alchemy, and Codex. `setView()` manages visibility and breadcrumb text; `renderSubView()` dispatches view renderers (lines 149–161). Their empty containers are already in **`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`** as `#view-techniques`, `#view-expeditions`, `#view-alchemy`, and `#view-codex` (lines 103–106).
- Actions use document-level delegation on `data-action` (lines 220–233), which is a good insertion point for combat, gathering, and crafting actions. `renderExpeditions()` / `startTrip()` / `collectTrip()` currently implement a single timed trip with stone rewards only (lines 128–139, 199–209).
- Alchemy is defined by `recipes` and `brew()` (lines 17–22, 141–144, 211–219). Recipes currently spend stones directly; there is no herb inventory or ingredient validation.
- **`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`** contains the existing panel/card and responsive systems. Reuse `.subview-layout`, `.content-panel`, `.expedition-card`, `.recipe`, and `.action-btn` patterns; add explicit styles for new enemy/health/path UI. The stylesheet is densely minified, with responsive overrides at `@media(max-width:1120px)`, `850px`, `650px`, and `390px` (lines 5–8).

### Best insertion points
- **Enemies and health/damage:** Add combat state to `defaultState()`, then render enemy/player health and combat controls in a dedicated view or in expeditions. Put combat resolution in dedicated functions near `startTrip()` / `collectTrip()`, dispatch via the existing `data-action` switch, and call `save(); render()` after state changes. Use `render()` or a dedicated renderer to keep health displays synchronized.
- **Sect system:** The sect is currently presentation-only: “Azure Cloud” and “Outer disciple” are hardcoded in `index.html`’s `.sect-card` (lines 29–35), and the breadcrumb’s `AZURE CLOUD SECT` is also static (line 42). Store sect/rank in `state` and render those labels dynamically. A sect view requires adding a nav entry, a view container, a `renderSubView()` branch, and a `setView()` breadcrumb label.
- **Herb gathering and pill crafting:** The expeditions list already includes “Gathering in the Mistwood” (`id: 'herbs'`), making it a natural gathering hook, but its completion currently awards only stones. Add itemized herb rewards to trip state/collection, display inventory in `renderAlchemy()`, and validate recipe ingredients in `brew()`. The current recipe copy explicitly says ingredients are included in stone cost, so update that alongside actual ingredient behavior.
- **Distinct body/spiritual paths:** Extend the state and progression model rather than relying on the current derived `body`/`spirit` display values. `techniques` already has a body-themed upgrade, but `state.upgrades.body` only increases breakthrough chance; `state.upgrades.array` currently drives the displayed spirit stat and stone yield. `render()`, `rateFor()`, breakthrough gating/effects, and the Codex description (“Body · Spirit · Qi”) are the main places to make those paths mechanically distinct and visible.

### Pitfalls
- `loadState()` merges saved state with defaults, but only specially deep-merges `upgrades` (line 34). New nested objects need explicit migration/default merging or old saves may leave them undefined.
- Offline progress in `loadState()` (lines 35–47) currently handles qi, stones, and daily counters only. Decide whether combat, herbs, or path progression should advance offline; don’t accidentally simulate combat from elapsed time without safeguards.
- `tick()` calls `render()` every second. Active subviews are rebuilt as HTML each tick, so keep event listeners delegated (as now) and avoid UI state stored only in DOM.
- Navigation is duplicated in desktop and mobile navs in `index.html` (lines 22–27 and 110–111); adding a view to only one leaves the other inconsistent. The sect card is separate static UI, not part of either nav.
- The sidebar `.sect-card` has fixed content and layout; dynamic sect names/ranks may need CSS handling for longer labels and mobile visibility.
